prompt: Flag hand-rolled expansions worse than an instruction the targets already have (`(x + 0.5).floor()` for round, `1/sqrt(x)` where rsqrt is meant, a compare-and-select emulating min/max), and hot-path instructions spent making an op match scalar IEEE behavior on edge cases — this codebase deliberately takes whatever the hardware instruction does (NaN handling, signed zeros, rounding ties) and does not promise scalar Rust's answer. Also flag a function returning a clamped value outside its documented domain where the contract is to return NaN: precision may be traded for speed, range never is.
